title: Encryption surface mapping and HSM fallback procedures
content:
Purpose:
This working document maps Redwood's encryption surfaces, defines a prioritized HSM fallback pattern for KMS failures, and prescribes auditable key rotation and evidence automation steps for compliance reviews. It is intended for eng infra, security, SRE, and customer onboarding leads responsible for BYOK and private deployments.

Scope:
- Encryption-at-rest across: control plane DBs, object store (S3-compatible), KV caches, ephemeral model caches, and tenant envelope keys.
- KMS variants: cloud-managed KMS, customer BYOK (tenant-keys), and HSM-backed appliances.
- Audit and SIEM export schema for rotation events and evidence snapshots.
- RBAC v2 controls for who can initiate or approve rotation and emergency key operations.

Assumptions and constraints:
- We support multiple HSM vendors; fallback must be vendor-agnostic.
- Rolling full-data re-encryption is expensive for large object stores. We prefer envelope-key rotation with lazy re-encryption when safe.
- All rotation operations require end-to-end audit events and cryptographic proof artifacts retained per compliance retention policy.

Key classes and mapping (encryption surface):
- Root (master) keys: stored in HSM or cloud KMS; used to encrypt intermediate/tenant keys.
- Envelope (tenant) keys: per-tenant or per-customer product key that encrypts data keys used in object store and DB columns.
- Data keys: short lived keys derived for encrypting blobs, cached in memory only.
- Exported artifacts: key-wrapping metadata, rotation logs, and proof-of-rotation digests.

Architecture notes (textual diagram):
- Control plane KMS/HSM cluster (primary) -> encrypts root/master keys -> wraps tenant envelope keys -> tenant envelope keys encrypt data keys used by worker nodes.
- Worker nodes cache wrapped data keys; they request unwrap operations via a routing proxy that enforces RBAC v2 policies and request quotas.

HSM fallback pattern (priority):
1) Normal: HSM primary (FIPS mode) serving Encrypt/Decrypt and Wrap/Unwrap.
2) Degraded: HSM read-only + cloud-KMS soft-unwrap for new requests (requires policy-based approval).
3) Emergency: Software KMS with key material exported (wrapped) and pinned into a secure vault with limited TTL for rotating back when HSM returns.

Fallback requirements and safety checks:
- Before switching to software KMS, verify: current HSM state, quorum signatures (2/3 infra leads), and that a snapshot of HSM logs has been exported to SIEM.
- Disable any automatic BYOK imports during fallback window.
- Emit audit event with fields (see Audit schema section) and attach HSM snapshot reference ID.

Key rotation types and triggers:
- Scheduled rotation: periodic (e.g., 365 days) for envelope keys, 90 days for data keys where applicable.
- Volume-triggered rotation: after N writes or M GB of data to a given envelope key.
- Compromise/incident rotation: immediate initiation when suspicious usage observed.
- Onboarding rotation: when moving a BYOK tenant from onboarding -> production.

High-level rotation flow (envelope key):
1) Pre-checks: verify backups, SIEM ingestion healthy, RBAC approval recorded.
2) Stage new key: create new envelope key in primary KMS/HSM; mark as pending.
3) Rewrap policy update: configure routing to prefer new wrappers for new data; existing wrapped objects remain addressable by old key until migrated.
4) Validation: run read/unwrap tests across a sample set (10k objects) and record digest proofs.
5) Gradual rewrap (lazy re-encryption): background job rewraps objects when touched or via batched migrators.
6) Final cutover: once migration progress >95% or after timebox, mark old key as retired and schedule secure destruction after retention window.
7) Evidence bundle: collect rotation log, proof digests, SIEM export, and key material lifecycle entries for compliance.

Rollback and emergency rollback:
- Keep old key in HSM in disabled state for at least retention period until evidence collected.
- If validation fails, roll back routing to old wrappers and initiate investigation.

Re-encryption strategies and tradeoffs:
- Lazy re-encryption: low-cost, consistent read availability; leaves old wrapped objects until touched. Good for large object stores and long tail access.
- Full re-encryption: immediate uniformity but high resource cost and possible downtime risk. Use only for sensitive short-lived caches or when policy requires.

RBAC v2 integration (who can do what):
- Roles: infra-admin, security-admin, compliance-auditor, tenant-admin (BYOK only for their keys), rotation-operator.
- Approvals: Scheduled rotations require 1 infra-admin; incident rotations require 2 approvers (infra-admin + security-admin) recorded in an approval ticket.
- Principle of least privilege: unwrap operations to HSM require a scope-limited token; long-lived credentials for unwrap are forbidden.

Audit log schema (required fields for every key lifecycle event):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- event_id (UUID)
- actor (email or service principal)
- actor_role (RBAC role)
- action (create|stage|promote|revoke|destroy|unwrap|wrap|fallback|fallback_revert)
- key_id (opaque id)
- key_type (root|envelope|data)
- key_version (string)
- cause (manual|scheduled|automated|incident)
- justification (human text or ticket id)
- success (true|false)
- error_message (if any)
- prev_key_id (if rotation)
- proof_digest (sha256 hex of a canonical proof bundle)
- evidence_bundle_ref (URL or artifact id exported to evidence store)
- hsm_snapshot_ref (if applicable)
- correlation_id (trace id)

SIEM export mapping (recommended indexes and field names):
- SIEM index: redwood-keys-YYYY.MM.DD
- mapped fields: timestamp->@timestamp, event_id->event.id, actor->user.name, actor_role->user.role, action->event.action, key_id->object.id, key_type->object.type, key_version->object.version, cause->event.cause, success->event.outcome, proof_digest->file.hash.sha256, evidence_bundle_ref->url, correlation_id->trace.id

Sample audit event (stringified example to be indexed):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-02-19T18:22:03Z",
  "event_id": "d9f3a6a2-7bfa-4c3e-b9d9-1b2a8f6b5c12",
  "actor": "infra-admin@redwood.ai",
  "actor_role": "infra-admin",
  "action": "promote",
  "key_id": "envkey-7b3f",
  "key_type": "envelope",
  "key_version": "v2",
  "cause": "scheduled",
  "justification": "annual rotation window 2026",
  "success": true,
  "proof_digest": "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08",
  "evidence_bundle_ref": "s3://evidence-prod/rotations/2026-02-19/envkey-7b3f-bundle.tar.gz",
  "correlation_id": "trace-91ab"
}

Evidence automation and retention process:
- On rotation completion the evidence automation job must produce: rotation.log (structured lines), proof_manifests.json (list of object_id -> old_wrapper -> new_wrapper -> proof_digest), and hsm_snapshot.tar.gz (if HSM involved).
- Evidence job uploads artifacts into the evidence S3 bucket with a path: evidence/{tenant}/{rotation-id}/ and emits the audit event above with evidence_bundle_ref.
- Retention: evidence artifacts kept for 7 years for enterprise customers requiring long-term audit. Shorter retention policies applied for other customers as per contract.

Automation hooks and playbooks (operational):
- rotation-orchestrator (k8s cronjob) triggers pre-checks and stages key creation.
- rewrap-workers (k8s autoscaled jobs) process lazy rewrap queues.
- evidence-exporter (lambda) bundles logs and pushes to evidence vault then calls SIEM API to index event.
- Emergency CLI: infra keyctl rotate-emergency --key envkey-7b3f --reason "hsm-failure" --approvers "alice,security-admin" (requires 2 approvers).

SIEM detection rules (examples):
- Alert if more than 3 rotations initiated for same key within 24h -> possible key compromise.
- Alert on failed evidence export where evidence_bundle_ref is missing 30m after rotation success.
- Alert if fallback to software KMS lasts > 4h without HSM snapshot present.

Validation and test plans:
- Unit tests: key create/promote/revoke happy path and failure modes.
- Integration tests: staged HSM outage simulated; ensure fallback flow emits correct audit events and evidence.
- Load tests: run lazy re-encryption workers against a 10M object sample and measure time/cost; verify proof manifest consistency.
- Security reviews: annual red-team on key lifecycle and HSM fallback flow.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Exact SLA for evidence-export (target: 10 minutes after rotation end) needs sign-off with compliance.
- Retention policy exceptions for regulated customers to be added to onboarding checklist.
- Standardize proof manifest canonical format with cryptographic signing by infra-root key.

Quick runbook (incident rotation):
1) PagerDuty alert -> rotation-operator acknowledges and creates JIRA incident (JIRA-####).
2) Run preflight checks: siem-ingest-health, hsm-status, backup-complete.
3) If HSM degraded -> follow HSM fallback pattern and emit fallback audit event.
4) Create new envelope key in HSM/cloud-KMS, stage, validate unwrap on sample.
5) Promote key, trigger background rewrap, and monitor proof-manifest entries.
6) When rotation job finishes, run evidence-exporter and verify SIEM indexing.

References and links:
- Confluence: Key Lifecycle Spec (linked above)
- Infra repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra (see /kms and /evidence-exporter)
- Oncall runbooks: /confluence/ops/oncall-rotation-playbooks
